clue.text: Secure fellow a weapon

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: An instruction, or a report, that a man has got hold of a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to fix or fasten it firmly in place, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Frightening retainer, say, protecting Arab in this way over month

indicators.note: protecting means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a retainer is an example of a fee, paid in advance to secure services

indicators.note: over means in this down entry one piece sits above the next

parts.note: Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
so means in this way, as in do it so

explanation.surface: A scary bodyguard shielding an Arab like this for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' suggests a servant but is a fee; 'protecting' wraps FEE around ARSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that inspires dread or alarm is terrifying, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Keep distinctive group with a role in staged production

parts.note: a set is a group
an actor's role in a play is a part

explanation.surface: A theatre company keeping its identity while taking a role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To set apart is to separate or distinguish, keeping a thing distinct from others.

clue.text: Record kept in recent era

indicators.note: kept in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A record set in the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across rec-ENT ER-a.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details in a ledger or log is to record them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: With no end of knowhow, ideal well trained footballer

with no means the letter that follows is dropped from the fodder words
end of picks the final letter of the word knowhow

explanation.surface: A footballer with perfect fitness but lacking the last bit of game intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no end of knowhow' removes W from IDEAL WELL; 'trained' rearranges the remaining IDEALELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dele Alli is an English midfielder who played for Tottenham Hotspur and England, so he is an example of a footballer.

clue.text: Minor player, one in unsettled state, right away being wasteful

parts.note: an extra is a minor player in a film

parts.note: a vagrant is someone wandering with no settled home

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor, homeless and unsettled, squandering money.
explanation.walkthrough: VAGRANT with 'right away' drops R to give VAGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending lavishly beyond need is wasteful, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: African mammal trampling flower that time forgot

indicators.note: trampling suggests letters trodden into disorder
forgot means a letter is left out of the word

explanation.surface: An animal crushing a bloom in a lost valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time forgot' takes T out of THAT, giving THA; 'trampling' rearranges FLOWERTHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the aardwolf, a hyena-like insect-eater of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: Collective wisdom about a hot Asian city

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: lore is the traditional knowledge of a group
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Traditional knowledge concerning a sweltering city in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province in Pakistan.

clue.text: Threaten to stop supporting young offender

to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A warning to cease backing a juvenile delinquent.
explanation.definitionFit: To be about to happen, looming menacingly, is to threaten, an intransitive verb sense.

clue.text: Smart person that's second in Paris occupying fantastic seat

indicators.note: occupying means one piece sits inside the other, as someone occupies a seat
fantastic suggests the letters of seat are made wildly different

parts.note: tu is the French second person singular pronoun, meaning you

explanation.surface: A clever someone in Paris sitting in an extraordinary chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges SEAT to ASTE, and 'occupying' puts the French pronoun inside it. 'Person' is grammatical person, not a human being.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of shrewd or clever, the adjective synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Joint faced by celebs putting vehicle in space?

parts.note: celebrities are stars
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.definitionFit: A craft built to travel among the stars is a spacecraft, the science-fiction word for a ship in space.

clue.text: Very brilliant body spun over wild area

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the words before it run out of order

explanation.surface: A dazzling object whirling over untamed territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SPUNOVER to SUPERNOV; A for area follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding star briefly outshines its whole galaxy, a celestial body of extreme brightness.

clue.text: Not wanting review of claim? I do in a realm of authority

parts.note: off means not wanting something, as in off one's food

indicators.note: review of suggests the letters are looked over again and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who would rather not have a claim looked at again by the bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of officials and its bureaucracy form a domain of power, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Flier, brave type ending in squadron

parts.note: a brave person is a hero

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word squadron

explanation.surface: A pilot, a courageous figure, completing service in an air force squadron.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird is something that flies, so it is a flier by example.

clue.text: Notice neckwear considerably restricted for actor

parts.note: a lot means considerably

explanation.walkthrough: A LOT 'restricted' loses its last letter, giving ALO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Ruffalo is an American film star who plays the Hulk in the Marvel films, an example of an actor.

clue.text: Broadcast by Republican expert in event round circuit?

parts.note: to relay is to broadcast
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A politician of the right broadcasting about an expert at an event.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race run in legs, often laps of a track, fits a contest held around a lap.

clue.text: Place for taking off other exotic clothing left in pieces principally

indicators.note: clothing means one piece is wrapped around the other
exotic suggests the letters made strange and rearranged
principally picks the first letter of each of the words in pieces

explanation.surface: A strip club scene: removing other unusual clothes, leaving them in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' turns OTHER into HEORT; 'clothing' wraps it around LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing pad where helicopters take off, a place for aircraft departure.

clue.text: Commercial man gets payment for follower

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
he is the pronoun for a man
rent is a regular payment

explanation.surface: An advertising man receives a fee for a devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of a cause or person is a follower, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Chance almost to transform fair nude for noted painter

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: luck is chance

indicators.note: to transform means the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist seizing the opportunity to make a pale nude into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: LUCK 'almost' is LUC; 'to transform' turns FAIRNUDE into IANFREUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucian Freud was a celebrated British figurative artist, known especially for his nudes, so a famous painter by example.

clue.text: Composer of quite lofty standing leaving hotel

parts.note: tallish means of fairly tall stature
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician of some eminence walking out of a hotel.

clue.text: Ordinary stretch of open land

definitions.meaning: an area of public grassland, such as a village green

explanation.surface: An everyday expanse of open countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both everyday and a piece of unenclosed public land.

clue.text: Game among some brings pain

indicators.note: among means one piece is set inside the other

Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Playing a game leaves some people hurting.

clue.text: Sanction arthouse works to tour Italy

indicators.note: to tour means one piece goes around another
works suggests the letters being worked into a new shape

explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges ARTHOUSE to AUTHORSE; 'to tour' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official permission for something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Element of hope raises work by Britten, maybe

indicators.note: element of means the letters are a part of the words that follow

explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across h-OPE RA-ises.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten wrote stage works such as Peter Grimes, so a sung drama is an example of his work.

clue.text: See doctor, retired doctor, in a yard in Italian region

clue.text: Young man, we hear, smiles — evidence of good weather?

parts.note: a son is a young man

explanation.surface: A cheerful lad grins, a sign that all is bright.

explanation.definitionFit: Rays of light from a bright sky show it is fine, so they are a sign of a fair day.

clue.text: Step taken by fool in decline?

explanation.surface: A misstep made by an idiot heading downhill.
